out_items.name: Certified Food Protection Manager

violations.title: Food Manager Certificate & Responsibility
violations.observation: There is no Certified Food Manager present in the establishment. The certified food managers certification expired on April 25, 2026 and is no longer valid.
violations.corrective_action: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager. It is highly suggested that you have more than one employee with the food manager's license. ORS Interactive, Inc. (see handout provided) issues the required photo identification card with proof of successful completion of a certified food manager's exam. Failure to have a certified food manager on site during ALL hours of operation including food preparation, food service, and cleaning/sanitizing of equipment/utensils will result in closure of the establishment. Provide a valid food manager certification within 10 days.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. There was no paper towels at the hand sink next to the cook line
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. One of the food employees corrected this during the inspection.

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at each handwashing sink. The hand sink next to the cook line did not have any hand soap. This is a repeat violation.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. The food employee corrected this during the inspection.

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed a dirty pan of water stored in the hand sink next to the cook line. This makes the hand sink hard to use.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. Discontinue storing any equipment or utensils enhancing. They are for washing hands only. Ensure that all hand sinks have soap and paper towel towels at all times.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Food Contact Surfaces Clean to Sight & Touch
violations.observation: The following equipment/utensils were observed soiled to sight and touch: several pieces of equipment in the drawers underneath the grill were not clean. Several plates and dishes on the service line were not clean and had mouse droppings on them.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to the sight and touch. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. Clean and sanitize all the plates and dishes on the serving line and all the utensils in the drawers underneath the grill. Correct as soon as possible or within 10 days. YUMMY KABOB (Inspection Date: 06/30/2026) Page 2 of 5

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: several foods in the walk-in refrigerator were not being held at the proper cold holding temperature. Cooked spinach was 47°, garbanzo beans were 50°, butter chicken was 47°, tzatziki sauce was 49°, garlic sauce was 47°, a bucket of “spices“ was 48°, 9 large pans of seasoned rice were 57°, 60°, and 58°, and a container of raw beef was 57°. The ambient temperature of the walk-in refrigerator was 59°.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. All the foods listed above were discarded due to temperature abuse.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. Observed a bottle of bleach stored with dry goods in the dry storage room.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. Chemical should not be stored with food. The food employee corrected this during the inspection.

violations.title: Poison/Toxic Material, Conditions of Use
violations.observation: Pesticides labeled for residential use were observed in the facility and are being applied by the operator to control pests. Observed at least three cans of Raid household/residential pesticides in the establishment, which is not approved.
violations.corrective_action: Remove residential use pesticides from the facility. When necessary for pest control, chemical pesticides must be applied by a certified pesticide applicator to prevent injury and contamination. Pest control must be done by a licensed pest control operator. Discard the cans of raid within three days. The PIC discarded all household pesticides during the inspection.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: nine large pans of cooked seasoned rice in the walk-in refrigerator that were made yesterday were out of temperature at 57°, 60°, 58°, 60° and other temperatures above 41°F. These pans were packed full, partially covered, and not cooled properly.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. Discontinue storing cooked foods in large covered pans to cool. They will not cool fast enough. The EHS discussed this with the PIC. The pans of rice were discarded due to temperature abuse.

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.title: Thermometers, Location for Units with TCS foods
violations.observation: There was no thermometer in the hot holding cabinet. Their previously was one, but it is no longer there.
violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. Provide a thermometer for this cabinet as soon as possible, or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed six months.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Controlling Pests, Inspect Premises
violations.observation: The premises is not being routinely inspected for the presence of insects, rodents and pests. This is evident based on the fact that there are mouse droppings in several areas of the establishment. There are also several flying insects in the establishment and dead insects on countertops and food equipment.
violations.corrective_action: Insects, rodents and pests are capable of transmitting disease to people by contaminating food and food-contact surfaces. Routinely inspect the premises to control the presence of insects, rodents and pests on the premises. The establishment needs to be inspected frequently to ensure there are no pest problems. Inspect the establish more frequently and clean up mouse, droppings, and dead insects. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

violations.title: Controlling Pests, Eliminate Harborage Conditions
violations.observation: Harborage conditions exist. There are at least three holes in walls, which may be allowing rodents to harbor in the establishment. These holes need to be sealed.
violations.corrective_action: Insects and other pests are capable of transmitting disease to people by contaminating food and food-contact surfaces. Eliminate harborage conditions to control and prevent the presence of pests on the premises. Inspect the establishment frequently to ensure that there are no holes or gaps in walls which could create a harborage condition for pests. Seal any holes or gaps found. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

violations.title: Openings Protected from Pest Entry
violations.observation: Windows or doors kept open for ventilation or other purposes do not have openings that are adequately protected against the entry of insects or rodents. There are several doors at the front and back the establishment that are left open for ventilation. These doors do not have screens installed. These doors are allowing pests such as flying insects and mice to gain access to the establishment. There were several live and dead insects observed in the establishment during this inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Windows or doors kept open for ventilation or other purposes shall have openings that are adequately protected against the entry of insects or rodents by 1) 16 mesh to 25.4mm (16 mesh to 1 inch) screens; 2) properly designed and installed air curtains to control flying insects; or 3) other effective means. Discontinue keeping doors open unless screens are installed. Keeping the doors open without screens installed is allowing pests to enter the establishment. Keep the doors closed or install screens and keep them closed. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection.

out_items.name: Personal cleanliness

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. All food employees must wear hair restraints or tie back their hair if long enough while working with food. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed six months.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items Storage and Handling
violations.observation: Observed several Styrofoam takeout containers on the counter over the steam table not being stored inverted and several of these had food debris and dead insects in them.
violations.corrective_action: Single service items should be stored upside down or in their plastic packaging to protect them from contamination. The food employee corrected this during the inspection by discarding the soiled containers and inverting the rest.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: the ambient air temperature of the walk-in refrigerator was 59°F and numerous foods in the unit were not at the proper holding temperature
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. Repair the walk-in refrigerator as soon as possible and discard all foods that are above 41°F most of which are listed elsewhere this report. YUMMY KABOB (Inspection Date: 06/30/2026) Page 3 of 5

out_items.name: Non-food contact surfaces clean

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The shelving over the steam table and refrigerator areas on the prep line was visibly soiled with food debris, dust and dead insects. The shelf was being used to store clean plates and Styrofoam takeout containers. The shelving also still had the protective shipping film on it. Most of the walk-in shelving is visibly soiled with food debris hanging on it and under it.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Clean the shelving in the prep areas and remove the protective shipping film; it is not intended for permanent use. Clean the shelving in the walk-in refrigerator as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection not to exceed six months.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Air Gap Provided
violations.observation: Observed the pre-wash spray hose to extend below the flood rim level of the sink basin at the 3-vat sink.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by providing an air gap as specified under 5-202.13. The spray hose at the 3-vat sink shall be altered to hang above the flood level rim of the 3-vat sink in order to provide an air gap. Adjust the length of the pre-wash spray hose so that it is above the flood level rim of the sink basin. Correct within three days.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: The backflow preventer on the mop sink is damaged and in need of repair. The bell cap is missing from the backflow prevention device. Also, there is a hose connected to the fixture which is too long.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. Disconnect the hose and remove it. Repair or replace the backflow preventer on the mop sink. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed a significant amount of food debris on the floor under and behind equipment under the hood, under and behind the steam table, in the small storage room, and behind and under tables and equipment.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. To effectively clean the establishment, equipment must be moved so that it can be cleaned under and behind. Clean all the areas listed above as soon as possible to remove all food debris, grease and grime.

violations.title: Premises Free of Litter
violations.observation: Observed an accumulation of litter on the exterior of the premises. There is an accumulation of litter in the back of the property which will attract pests and could contribute to a mouse problem.
violations.corrective_action: Remove all litter from the premises to allow for regular and effective cleaning and to prevent harborage conditions. Clean up all the litter on the ground of the establishment as soon as possible or within 30 days.

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: The ambient temperature of the kitchen especially in front of the cooking equipment seemed to be very hot. The ventilation system in the hood over the cooking area sounded as if it was running, but a check of it showed that it was not drawing any air.
violations.corrective_action: Repair the physical facilities. Poor repair and maintenance compromises the functionality of the physical facilities. Have the hood system checked and repaired as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection.

violations.title: Floor to Wall Junctures Coved, Closed
violations.observation: Floor and wall junctures are not coved. There are several places where the floor walls junctures are damaged or deteriorated and may be allowing pests to enter into or harbor in the establishment.
violations.corrective_action: If cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no more than 1 millimeter. Repair all the holes in the walls and ensure that all floor wall junctures are sealed.

out_items.name: Adequate ventilation and lighting, designated areas used

violations.title: Protective Shielding on Light Bulbs
violations.observation: Observed there are a few lightbulbs in the kitchen and food prep area ceiling fixtures that do not have appropriate shielding installed.
violations.corrective_action: All light bulbs in food preference storage areas must be shielded. Provide lightbulb shielding as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

violations.title: Dressing Rooms/Lockers, Designated
violations.observation: A pair of employee sneakers was stored on food shelving next to food in the dry storage area.
violations.corrective_action: Instruct employees to use the designated dressing rooms to prevent contamination of food, food equipment and utensils, and preparation surfaces. Discontinue allowing employees to store their personal belongings with foods. Please designate a storage area away from food and food equipment for employees to store their belongings. The employee moved the shoes during the inspection.

out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: DOK Clean Facility
violations.observation: There is no certified food manager on duty and the person in charge was unable to describe the relationship between the prevention of foodborne disease and the oversight of maintaining a clean food establishment. Observed several unclean food and non-food contact surfaces throughout the establishment. The establishment does not appear to be getting cleaned as often as necessary, especially considering the recent complaint.
violations.corrective_action: The person in charge shall understand that employees shall be cleaning and sanitizing all equipment, utensils, and surfaces as needed to prevent the spread of bacteria. The EHS spoke with the person in charge about cleaning more frequently, implementing a clean as you go strategy, and keeping the establishment clean as clean as possible, considering the recent complaint of mice in the establishment.

violations.title: Permit to Operate Posted in Conspicuous Location
violations.observation: The establishment has not posted the permit to operate in a conspicuous location.
violations.corrective_action: A valid permit shall be posted in every food establishment in a conspicuous place in the public view. Food establishment permits are issued for a calendar year and expire on December 31 regardless of the month of issue. Post the permit in a conspicuous location where customers can see it by the follow up. YUMMY KABOB (Inspection Date: 01/02/2026) Page 4 of 5

out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: A food employee was observed drinking from a bottle of water directly in the food prep area where it may contaminate food, clean equipment, utensils or other items needing protection.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may only eat, drink, or use tobacco in a designated area like a dining room or office area. Employees shall not eat or drink in the kitchen areas, warewashing areas, or storage areas where items may become contaminated. If drinking in the food prep area, be sure to be drinking from a covered cup with a straw.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. There were no paper towels available at one of the hand sinks in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing.

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: A large stainless steel insert full of water was in the patio bar area hand sink, making it difficult to wash hands.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. Do not store equipment in hand sinks, and keep hand sinks accessible at all times so employees can wash their hands. Correct by the follow-up.

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at each handwashing sink. There was no hand soap available at one of the hand sinks in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands.

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. Each hand sink must have a sign that says employees must wash hands. There were no such signs in the men’s and women’s restrooms. There is also no sign at the sink in the patio bar area.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. Post the required handwashing signage in the men’s and women’s restrooms and the patio bar area by the follow-up.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Food Contact Surface, Clean after Use
violations.observation: Equipment food-contact surfaces/utensils were not observed cleaned before any possible contamination. The following food contact surfaces need to be cleaned: - The orange juicer in the patio bar area was found to be filled with orange peels and did not appear to have been cleaned since the last time it was used before the day of inspection. - Several kebab skewers were stored in the clean skewer bucket, but were not clean. - There were two blenders that the manager said weren’t being used, but they were still dirty from the last time they were used.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned at any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred. All equipment should be cleaned (washed, rinsed, and sanitized) after it is used. Correct by the follow-up. The manager began cleaning these items during the inspection.

violations.title: Chemical Sanitization, Chlorine Requirements
violations.observation: When tested, the low temperature, chemical sanitizing warewashing machine was observed with a sanitizing rinse concentration of less than 50 ppm chlorine solution.
violations.corrective_action: Immediately discontinue use of the dishmachine. Until the machine is adequately repaired, set up the three-compartment sink to manually wash, rinse and sanitize food-contact surfaces using a sanitizing solution at the proper concentration of at least 50 to 200 ppm total chlorine. The EHS primed the pump and got the sanitizer concentration to 50 ppm during the inspection. The EHS also showed the manager how to prime the dishwasher and advised to check it daily.

out_items.name: Proper hot holding temperatures

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: two pans of cooked lamb in the hot holding unit were 125°F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. The lamb was reheated to 165°. Do not using the hot holding unit to reheat foods. Foods must be reheated in the microwave, on the stove, or in the oven to the proper temperature (165º for foods prepared on site) within 2 hours, and then placed in the hot holding unit to keep hot at 135° or above.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: whole milk in the refrigerator in the patio bar area was 48°. Unsalted butter in the same unit was 48°. The unit was unplugged and not working.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. The milk and the unsalted butter were discarded due to temperature abuse.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: there were several foods prepared on site such as butter chicken, basmati rice, white rice, and other foods that are not being date marked.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. The EHS discussed the date marking requirements with the person in charge. Start date marking foods immediately and have all food date marked by the follow up.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. There were several instances of chemicals being stored improperly with food or food equipment to include in the patio bar area, and in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. The EHS discussed the proper way to store chemicals to prevent contamination of food with the person in charge. The food manager had staff begin moving the chemicals during the visit. YUMMY KABOB (Inspection Date: 01/02/2026) Page 2 of 5

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.title: Thermometers, Location for Units with TCS foods
violations.observation: Observed the thermometer on the hot holding unit was not working, and there was no thermometer inside the unit.
violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. Provide and install a thermometer for the hot holding unit by the follow up.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Controlling Pests, Pest Control Methods
violations.observation: The person in charge has a pest control contractor working in the establishment to eliminate pests, however, there are mouse droppings in the dry storage area of the kitchen and in the hookah storage room next to the patio bar. Also, food debris was observed in several places on the floor, as well as standing water, which will not help to prevent pest problems.
violations.corrective_action: Insects and other pests are capable of transmitting disease to people by contaminating food and food-contact surfaces. If pests are found on the premises methods shall be used to control their presence. Frequently cleaning up food debris from the floor, and keeping the floors, clean and dry will help with pest problems. Mouse droppings need to be cleaned up so that the problem can be effectively monitored. The EHS discussed these practices with the person in charge. Correct by the follow-up.

violations.title: Openings Protected from Pest Entry
violations.observation: Observed gaps at the bottoms of the two front doors and the rear door to the patio. Also, the door between the patio and the dining room room was left open, which would allow pests to enter from the outside through the door gaps and the open door.
violations.corrective_action: Fill or close holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings to protect against the entry of insects and rodents. The EHS discussed with the person in charge that door gaps must be sealed to prevent and pressed entry and that the back door to the patio, which was in repair must be repaired to prevent pest entry. Correct by the follow-up.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Observed cases of chicken stored on the floor in the walk-in. Observed large bags of rice stored on the floor in the kitchen while the kitchen floor was dirty and wet. Observed bottled water, sugar and a case of oranges on the floor in the patio area bar.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. The person in charge stated that the foods had just been delivered. The rice was moved off the floor during the inspection. Move the chicken, sugar, oranges, and bottled water and all other food items stored on the floor off the floor as soon as possible. Correct by the follow-up.

out_items.name: Personal cleanliness

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: One of the food employees was not wearing a hair restraint when preparing foods.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. All food handlers must wear effective hair restraints, or if their hair is long enough, tie it back to prevent it from getting into food. The food employee put a hat on during the inspection.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: in the patio bar area, the ice scoop handle was stored inside the ice in the ice bin. Observed knives being stored between the steam table and the prep refrigerator in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. Do not store utensils between equipment. The surfaces are not clean.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils Self-Draining Position/Covered/Inverted
violations.observation: Observe the single service Styrofoam containers, not being stored inverted as required.
violations.corrective_action: Store all single service upside down to prevent prevent contamination. The manager corrected this during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: Clean Linens Free of Food Residues/Soil
violations.observation: In the patio bar area, clean glasses were stored on linens, and the linens were visibly soiled.
violations.corrective_action: Clean linens shall be free from food residues and other soiling matter. Remove the soiled linens and store clean glasses on clean surfaces to keep the glasses clean.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Cutting Board, When to Resurface or Discard
violations.observation: The cutting board along the main prep refrigerator is heavily scratched and scored and stained. The food contact surface is no longer easily cleaned and sanitized due to condition.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces such as cutting blocks and boards that are subject to scratching and scoring shall be resurfaced if they can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized, or discarded if they are not capable of being resurfaced. Replace or resurface to cutting board by the follow up. YUMMY KABOB (Inspection Date: 01/02/2026) Page 3 of 5

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following equipment is not operating properly and/or is in poor repair: the chemical sanitizing dish machine was not working properly. A bottle of bleach was connected to the supply tube, which is not common.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. Have the dish machine checked by your vendor to ensure that it is set up and working properly by the follow up.

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Hard Wood
violations.observation: Observed food being served on a wooden plate/platter.

Discontinue serving food on wooden equipment. Correct by the follow up.

out_items.name: Non-food contact surfaces clean

violations.title: Air Gaps/Breaks
violations.observation: Observed the sprayer head at the warehouse washing machine hanging too low and into the sink.
violations.corrective_action: An air gap between the water supply inlet and the flood level rim of the plumbing fixture, equipment, or nonfood equipment shall be at least twice the diameter of the water supply inlet and may not be less than one inch. The manager hung the sprayer head above the top of the sink during the inspection. Adjust a sprayer heads so that it hangs above the top of the sink, not in the sink, by the follow up.

violations.title: Outside Receptacle, Tight Fitting Lids

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Premises Free of Litter

violations.corrective_action: Remove all litter from the premises to allow for regular and effective cleaning and to prevent harborage conditions. Clean up as much as the litter as possible before the follow up.

violations.title: Premises Free of Unnecessary Items/Equipment

violations.corrective_action: Remove unnecessary items, including equipment which is no longer in use, from the premises to allow for regular and effective cleaning and to prevent harborage conditions. Please have all the unused access equipment removed within six months.

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Observed the hood system was not being operated and excessive heat and smoke in the establishment. The hood system is not being operated due to the noise it generates, which was excessive.
violations.corrective_action: Repair the physical facilities. Poor repair and maintenance compromises the functionality of the physical facilities. The hood must be operated to prevent heat. Smoke in grease buildup in the establishment. The manager has ordered a part to correct a problem. Correct a problem and use the hood system as soon as possible. out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' FACILITY DID NOT HAVE AN EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY IN PLACE AT BEGINNING OF INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. FACILITY SIGNED COPIES OF THE POLICY DURING INSPECTION AND UNDERSTANDS SIGNED COPIES SHOULD BE KEPT ONSITE AT THE ESTABLISHMENT.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS GAVE PIC A COPY OF CLEANUP PROCEDURE DURING INSPECTION. YUMMY KABOB (Inspection Date: 07/22/2025) Page 3 of 5

violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. PIC UNDERSTANDS PROPER HANDWASHING PROCEDURES MUST BE REVIEWED WITH EMPLOYEES AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. HANDWASHING SINKS MUST BE ACCESSIBLE AND OPERATING BEFORE REQUESTING A FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION TO REOPEN. YUMMY KABOB (Inspection Date: 07/22/2025) Page 2 of 5

out_items.name: Proper cooling time and temperature

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 70F, No More than 2 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety foods are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours: OBSERVED CHICKPEAS AT 57-60F AND COOKED CHICKEN AT 54F IN LARGE HOME DEPOT BUCKETS MADE THE DAY PRIOR TO INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. PIC DISCARDED OF FOODS. PROPER COOLING PARAMETERS WERE DISCUSSED WITH THE PIC. PLEASE ENSURE COOLING FOODS ARE NOT STORED IN LARGE PORTIONS WITH LIDS.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: OBSERVED IMPROPERLY COOLING LARGE PORTIONS OF FOOD IN BUCKETS AND LARGE BULK CONTAINERS IN THE WALK-IN COOLER WITH LIDS.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS DISCUSSED PROPER COOLING METHODS WITH THE PIC. PLEASE ENUSRE CONTINUED CORRECTION.

violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing utensils improperly stored between use as follows: OBSERVED BOWLS STORED DIRECTLY IN VARIOUS FOOD ITEMS THROUGHOUT BACK KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED PROPER DISPENSING UTENSIL STORAGE WITH PIC; PLEASE ENSURE DISPENSING UTENSILS STORED IN FOOD HAVE A HANDLE.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw lamb over tomatoes.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CFM re arranged items.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: raw chicken over raw beef and lamb.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). CFM re arranged items.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Chemical Sanitization, Chlorine Requirements
violations.observation: When tested, the chlorine-based sanitizing solution was observed to be at a concentration less than what is required for effective sanitization of food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils. Observed the sanitizing solution in the 3 vat sink with a concentration of 50 ppm total chlorine.
violations.corrective_action: A chlorine-based sanitizing solution shall have a minimum concentration of at least 50 to 200 ppm total chlorine when tested using the appropriate test kit. CFM adjusted concentration.

violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment were not observed sanitized: stainless steel prep table being used for prep that came into direct contact with raw ground beef. Observed washed with soap and not sanitized with bleach solution.
violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. CFM sanitized with bleach solution.

out_items.name: Proper cooking time and temperatures

violations.title: Cooking Raw Animal Foods, Minimum of 165F
violations.observation: The following poultry item was not cooked to a sufficient temperature and/or time to eliminate pathogenic bacteria: chicken on the outer layer of the rotating shawarma rack observed at 136f.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods such as poultry, wild game animals, stuffed fish, stuffed meat, stuffed pasta, stuffed poultry, stuffed ratites, or stuffing containing any of these raw animal foods shall be cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 165F for at least 15 seconds. CFM increased flame to cook to 165f.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: chicken on shawarma rack.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. CFM marked with discard time.

violations.title: Time as a Public Health Control, Written Procedures
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide written procedures for the use of time as a public health control with the following time/temperature control for safety food item(s): chicken on shawarma rotating rack. Since item is not fully cooked on the inside, it must be cooked and sold or discarded within 4 hours and must be held on TPHC, requiring written procedures.
violations.corrective_action: If time only is used as a public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety food before cooking or for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that is displayed or held for service for immediate consumption, written procedures shall be prepared in advance and maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request. Provided written procedures and revised with CFM.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.observation: Food stored in a wet or soiled location as follows: boxes of dough stored on wet floor, causing box to become soiled.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food in a clean, dry location.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: spoons stored in rice and falafel with the handle touching the food and using bowls as scoops.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. CFM removed above items from the food.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer containers of tahini sesame were observed reused for the storage of raw chicken in the WIR.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. YUMMY KABOB (Inspection Date: 01/17/2025) Page 3 of 4

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Durable Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not resistant to corrosion: orange Home Depot buckets are not food grade and are not designed to be durable.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. Please do not use Home Depot buckets for food storage.

out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Test Kit/Device for Chemical Sanitizer
violations.observation: There is no test kit located in the facility for monitoring the concentration of the chemical sanitizing solutions. Observed that the test kit had been soaked with water, making it un usable.
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a new bleach test kit.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed that the floors, walls, and ceilings in the kitchen are in need of cleaning. Observed accumulation of dirt, grease, and debris in all areas of the kitchen including inside the WIR and dry storage area.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food.
